context.storage: The user is currently viewing storage «{path}» (storageId: {storageId}).
context.cell: The user is currently viewing cell «{cell}» of storage «{path}». «{cell}» is the cell's grid address (row {row}, column {col}); its storageId is {storageId}. When the user says "this cell"/"the selected cell", they mean cell «{cell}» — always refer to it by that name.

list_storages.description: Returns a flat list of all storage cells/containers with their metadata: name, location, grid size (gridRows/gridCols), position within the parent cell (the cellAddress field — a ready-made address, e.g. "B3"), component count. Use it to find the needed storage before calling other tools. Cell addressing: letter = column (A=column 0, B=column 1, …), number = row (row 0 → 1); the cell at row 0, column 0 is "A1". Always use ready-made addresses (cellAddress from tool responses or the page context), do not compute them yourself.

get_storage_details.description: Returns detailed information about a single storage cell: its child cells (children), the list of components (components), grid dimensions and spans (merged cells). Every component and child cell has a cellAddress field (e.g. "A1") — use it as the address, do NOT compute the address yourself. Use it when you already know the storageId.

params.storageId: Unique identifier of the storage cell (storage ID)

get_storage_components.description: Returns the list of the storage's components/parts. Each component includes a cellAddress field — a ready-made cell address (e.g. "A1"). ALWAYS take the address from cellAddress, do NOT compute it yourself. Without a cell specified — recursively across the whole storage. To get the contents of ONE cell, pass its address in the cell field (e.g. "A1") — this is the preferred way. The address of the cell selected by the user and the storageId are available in the current page context — use them directly. Cell addressing: letter = column (A=column 0, B=column 1, …), number = row (row 0 → 1); the cell at row 0, column 0 is "A1". Always use ready-made addresses (cellAddress from tool responses or the page context), do not compute them yourself.

params.storageId: Identifier of the storage cell (storage ID).
params.cell: Address of a specific grid cell, e.g. "A1" or "B3" (letter=column, number=row). The preferred way to choose a cell. Optional.
params.row: Alternative to cell: the row number (0-based). Specify together with col. Optional.
params.col: Alternative to cell: the column number (0-based). Specify together with row. Optional.

create_storage.description: Creates a new storage cell (drawer, shelf, container). You can specify a name, a physical location, a parent cell (parentId) and a position in the parent's grid — preferably via the parentCell address (e.g. "B1"). If an internal grid is needed, specify gridRows and gridCols. Cell addressing: letter = column (A=column 0, B=column 1, …), number = row (row 0 → 1); the cell at row 0, column 0 is "A1". Always use ready-made addresses (cellAddress from tool responses or the page context), do not compute them yourself.

params.name: Name of the new storage cell (e.g. "Drawer A1", "Top shelf")
params.parentId: ID of the parent storage cell if a nested container is being created. Optional.
params.parentCell: Address of the parent grid cell into which the container is placed (e.g. "B1"). The preferred way to specify the position. Optional.
params.parentRow: Alternative to parentCell: the row number (0-based) in the parent's grid. Specify together with parentCol. Optional.
params.parentCol: Alternative to parentCell: the column number (0-based) in the parent's grid. Specify together with parentRow. Optional.
params.gridRows: Number of rows in this cell's internal grid. Defines that the cell is divided into sections. Optional.
params.gridCols: Number of columns in this cell's internal grid. Optional.

update_storage.description: Updates a storage cell's metadata: name, location, the link to the parent cell and the position in its grid (preferably via the parentCell address, e.g. "B1"). Unlike update_storage_grid, it allows changing any fields, not only the grid size. Cell addressing: letter = column (A=column 0, B=column 1, …), number = row (row 0 → 1); the cell at row 0, column 0 is "A1". Always use ready-made addresses (cellAddress from tool responses or the page context), do not compute them yourself.

params.storageId: Identifier of the storage cell to update
params.name: New name of the storage cell. Optional.
params.parentId: New parent cell ID (to move the container). Optional.
params.parentCell: New cell address in the parent's grid (e.g. "B1"). The preferred way. Optional.
params.parentRow: Alternative to parentCell: the new row number (0-based). Specify together with parentCol. Optional.
params.parentCol: Alternative to parentCell: the new column number (0-based). Specify together with parentRow. Optional.

update_storage_grid.description: Updates the size of a storage cell's internal grid (number of rows and columns). Use it to set or change how a drawer/container is split into sections.

params.storageId: Identifier of the storage cell (storage ID)
params.rows: Number of rows in the storage grid
params.cols: Number of columns in the storage grid

merge_storage_grid_cells.description: Merges several adjacent grid cells into one (like "merge cells" in Excel/spreadsheets). The selected cells must form a rectangle; the top-left corner is set by the startCell address (e.g. "A1") — preferably, or by the startRow/startCol pair. Use it to create custom-size sections inside a drawer/container. Cell addressing: letter = column (A=column 0, B=column 1, …), number = row (row 0 → 1); the cell at row 0, column 0 is "A1". Always use ready-made addresses (cellAddress from tool responses or the page context), do not compute them yourself.

params.storageId: Identifier of the storage cell whose grid cells need to be merged
params.startCell: Address of the top-left cell of the rectangle to merge (e.g. "A1"). The preferred way. Optional if startRow/startCol are set.
params.startRow: Alternative to startCell: the first row number of the rectangle (0-based)
params.startCol: Alternative to startCell: the first column number of the rectangle (0-based)

split_storage_grid_cell.description: Splits a previously merged grid cell back into separate cells (like "unmerge" in Excel). To get the spanId, first call get_storage_details and find the needed span in the gridSpans field.

params.storageId: Identifier of the storage cell whose grid contains the merged cell to split
params.spanId: Unique identifier of the merged cell (span). Get it from get_storage_details → gridSpans[].id

delete_storage_cell.description: Deletes a storage cell. WARNING: Destructive action — all components attached to this cell will lose their location. Child cells are also deleted cascadingly.

params.storageId: Identifier of the storage cell to delete

errors.missingRectangleStart: Specify the start of the rectangle: startCell (e.g. "A1") or a startRow/startCol pair.
errors.invalidStorageRef: Not a valid storage reference: "{ref}". Expected a storage id or a "mk://storages/storage/<id>" reference.
